summary: Year 2 children recognise and use the £ and p symbols, read and say amounts of money two ways (150p and 'one pound and fifty pence'), and combine coins to make a stated target amount by tracking value. The central notation rule is that £ and p are never written together: '£1.50p' is wrong — write 150p, or £1 and 50p, or £1.50. At Year 2 pounds and pence are recorded separately and the same amount has more than one correct written form (150p is the same money as £1 and 50p). Taught through real shop/price contexts, listening for correct use rather than asking for symbol definitions.
misconceptions: Muddles the two symbols or which side the symbol goes
Reads 150p and £1 and 50p as different amounts (misses the equivalence)
When combining coins, counts the number of coins rather than their value toward the total

activities.title: Build a price with coins and record it correctly
steps: Look at a price tag (e.g. 75p, or £1 and 50p) and choose real or on-screen coins to make exactly that amount
Say the running total by VALUE as each coin is added — e.g. '50... 70... 75' — not by the number of coins
Write the amount down in a correct form, then write it a second way if possible (150p / £1 and 50p)
Check your written amount against the rule: never put £ and p together
activities.insight: An amount of money can be built from coins by adding their values to a target, and the same amount has more than one correct written form, but £ and p are never written together.

activities.title: Shop role-play: pay, read tags and spot a wrong price
steps: Take part in a shop/market-stall exchange where a shopkeeper names a price ('one pound and fifty pence') and asks you to make and hand over that amount in coins
Read a price tag aloud (e.g. read '150p' and offer an equivalent spoken form)
Judge a price written as '£1.50p': say whether it looks right and explain what is wrong with it
activities.insight: Money language is used in context — reading, saying and paying amounts — and a confident user flags '£1.50p' as wrongly written because £ and p should not appear together.

activities.title: Match and write amounts; catch the notation error
steps: Write a given price (e.g. hear '75p' spoken, write the amount) using correct notation
Match a spoken or written form to its equivalent: draw a line from '150p' to '£1 and 50p'
Combine coins to reach a stated total such as 75p (e.g. 50p + 20p + 5p)
Decide whether '£1.50p' is written correctly and, if not, rewrite it
activities.insight: Recognising correct notation and equivalent forms, and selecting coins that sum to a target, consolidate the rule that £ and p are recorded separately.

checkQuestion: In a shopping context, listen for correct USE (never ask the child to define a symbol): (1) Show a price written '150p': 'Read this price to me', then 'Can you write it another way?' (2) 'I want to buy something that costs 75p — use these coins to make 75p and tell me the total as you go.' (3) Show '£1.50p' written down: 'Does this look right to you? Read it.' Listen for correct reading, the £/p equivalence, and whether they flag £ and p written together.
checkAnswer: Reads the price correctly and offers an equivalent form (150p is £1 and 50p); combines coins to make 75p while tracking the value (not the count); recognises '£1.50p' as wrongly written because £ and p should not appear together.
